Privacy Policy

Last updated: 21 October 2026

Timewarp runs on your computer. Your files, saved passwords and browser data stay there. To do a task, your agent sends your request and the content it's working with to an AI model provider. We keep your account, your billing records and, unless you turn on Privacy Mode, a copy of your chat history and of your agents, memory, skills and settings, so they follow you to your other computers. If you use Agent ID, we also keep your agents' identities, what they send and receive, and the outcome of your identity check, so every agent can be traced to the person or business responsible for it. That data is stored in the EU. We don't sell your data, use it for advertising, or train AI models on it.

1. Who we are

TimeWarp (“we”, “us”) provides the Timewarp app and website and is the controller of the personal data described in this policy. Contact us at support@timewarpdev.com.

2. What this policy covers

This policy covers the Timewarp desktop app for Windows and macOS, your Timewarp account, Agent ID (its dashboard, API, MCP server, command-line tool and developer kit), our emails and support, and the website timewarpdev.com. The Cookie Policy covers cookies on the website.

Websites and apps that your agent uses on your behalf have their own privacy policies. So do Google, OpenAI, GitHub and Microsoft when you sign in or download through them.

3. What stays on your computer

The app keeps the following on your computer only. We don't receive it and can't see it:

  • Your workspace files and any files you give your agents.
  • The vault: passwords, cards and other secrets, encrypted with your operating system's key store (Windows DPAPI or the macOS Keychain). Card security codes are never saved.
  • Browser profiles, cookies, history and saved sites in the built-in browser.
  • Your sign-ins to ChatGPT and to MCP servers, and MCP servers that run a command on your computer.
  • Automations, which run on the computer they were made on.
  • The app's technical log. It doesn't contain your messages or content.

Your agents, their memory and daily notes, skills and some settings are kept on your computer and, unless you turn on Privacy Mode, also synced to your account (section 4). When several accounts use the same computer, each account's data is kept apart.

Keeping data locally doesn't mean it never leaves your computer. When your agent works on a task, the content it needs goes to an AI model provider (section 5). When it uses a website or app for you, that service receives what the agent sends it.

The desktop app doesn't send us analytics, usage tracking or crash reports.

To limit abuse, our servers use your IP address in memory for rate limiting and don't store it. Before a request reaches an AI model, our servers check it for card numbers, private keys and API keys and reject it if they find any. This check isn't perfect, so please don't paste secrets into chats.

We don't make decisions about you based solely on automated processing that have legal or similarly significant effects.

5. AI model providers

To answer you, the model needs your message plus the context for the task. That can include earlier messages in the conversation, your agent's memory and instructions, content from files or web pages the agent is working with, and the results of its actions. Chat titles and memory notes are written by the same provider. Which provider receives this depends on how the request is paid for.

On Timewarp credits

  • GPT models and dictation: Microsoft, through the Azure OpenAI Service.
  • Claude models: Anthropic. Anthropic receives a pseudonymous account ID, not your name or email address.

These requests pass through our servers on the way to the provider. We don't store their content. We keep only the usage record described above. Microsoft and Anthropic process the content for us under their business terms. Those terms don't allow them to train models on it. They may keep it for a limited time to detect abuse.

On your own ChatGPT plan

On the Free plan, you can connect your ChatGPT account. The app then sends requests directly from your computer to OpenAI, and they don't pass through our servers. Your OpenAI sign-in stays on your computer. OpenAI handles these requests as the provider of your ChatGPT plan, under its own terms and privacy policy. Your ChatGPT data controls decide whether OpenAI may use the content to improve its models.

6. Connected apps

If you connect apps such as Gmail, Slack, Notion or GitHub, our partner Composio handles the authorisation and stores the access tokens. When you ask, your agent reads or acts in those apps through Composio. We pass on only what's needed for the action you requested. Each app's own privacy policy also applies. You can disconnect an app at any time.

7. Agent ID

Agent ID gives your AI agents an identity and their own mail address, phone number, wallet, virtual card and virtual machine, and lets other services check that an agent has a verified owner. The Agent ID Terms apply when you use it.

DataWhy we use itLegal basis (GDPR)
Your agents' identities: names, handles, the app each agent runs in, keys (stored only as hashes), signing keys, limits and settings, and which account and organisation each agent belongs to.To run Agent ID, and so each agent can be traced to the person or business responsible for it.Contract; our legitimate interest in keeping agents accountable (Art. 6(1)(f))
Identity verification (KYC): our partner Stripe checks a photo of your ID document and a selfie. We receive the result, your name as it appears on the document, and your country. We don't receive or keep the document or the selfie.To verify who is responsible for your agents, which live wallets and some other features require.Your explicit consent for the biometric check (Art. 9(2)(a)), which you give before the check starts; contract; legitimate interest in traceability and preventing fraud
Business verification (KYB): the business's legal name, registration number, VAT number, country and website, its registration document, the name and role of the verified person who submits it, and, for EU businesses, the result of checking the VAT number in the EU's VAT register (VIES), which returns the name and address it is registered to.To verify the business responsible for an organisation's agents.Contract; legitimate interest in traceability and preventing fraud
What your agents send and receive: emails and their attachments, text messages, call details and voicemail recordings, contacts your agents save, wallet transfers and addresses, card applications, and commands run on their machines with their output.To deliver these services to your agents and show you what they did.Contract
People your agents deal with: the email addresses, phone numbers, wallet addresses and message content of people who write to, call or pay your agents, or whom your agents contact.To deliver the messages, calls and payments. You decide what your agents do, and you're responsible for having a lawful basis for it.Our legitimate interest in providing the service you instruct (Art. 6(1)(f))
Activity log: who did what and when, such as an agent sending a message or money, a key being created, or a service checking an agent's passport.To keep agents accountable, investigate misuse and answer lawful requests.Legitimate interest in traceability and security; legal obligation where it applies (Art. 6(1)(c))

Passports. When your agent proves its identity to another service, the passport tells that service the agent's ID and name, whether its owner is verified, and, for a verified business, the business's name. A verified person's name is never shared. The service gets a pseudonymous owner reference that is different for every service, so services can't link your agents across them.

Traceability. We keep the link between each agent and its owner so that someone is responsible for what the agent does. We disclose an owner's identity only when the law requires it, for example on a court order or a request from an authority, or when necessary to protect people from serious harm.

Getting an Agent ID from a link. If you open a link an agent shows you, we use the email address you enter to send you a one-time code, and once you confirm it we create your Timewarp account with it (or sign you in to the one you have).

Wallets. Agent wallets are held with our partner Privy on the Base blockchain. If you buy USDC with a card, MoonPay (or, in the US, Stripe) processes that purchase and the details you give it, under its own privacy policy. We send MoonPay the wallet's address, your email address and your account's ID, so the money lands in the right wallet and the purchase can be traced to you. Wallet addresses and transfers on a public blockchain are visible to anyone and can't be deleted.

Bank transfers. Bank deposits and withdrawals go through Bridge, a Stripe company. Where Bridge offers bank transfers, its identity check is the one we use too: we send Bridge your email address (and your name, if we have it), Bridge checks your ID and a selfie under its own terms and privacy policy, and tells us the outcome with your name and country. When you verify an organisation, Bridge checks the business (its registration, its owners and its documents) the same way, and tells us the outcome. When you add money by SEPA, you choose the amount and Bridge gives the details to send it to. The bank account details you enter go straight on to Bridge. We keep only the bank's name, the last four characters of the account, and the amount and state of each transfer.

9. Transfers outside the EU

Some of our providers process data outside the EU/EEA, mainly in the United States. When they do, we rely on the EU–US Data Privacy Framework if the provider is certified under it. Otherwise we use the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses, with extra safeguards where needed. Email us for a copy of the safeguards that apply.

10. How long we keep data

  • Account, organisation, chat history, and synced agents, memory, skills and settings: while your account exists. After you ask us to delete your account, we delete this data within 30 days.
  • Payment and accounting records, including the usage behind a charge: for seven years after the end of the financial year, as the Swedish Bookkeeping Act requires.
  • Other usage records: while your account exists.
  • Shares: what you shared is deleted when the member accepts or declines it, or when you cancel it. A share that isn't answered expires after 30 days, and its content is deleted after that. The record of who shared what with whom is kept while your account exists.
  • Invitations: they expire after 14 days. We delete them with the organisation or when you ask.
  • Support requests and email delivery records: as long as we need them to help you and handle follow-up questions, and no longer than two years after the case is closed.
  • Agent ID mail, texts, calls, recordings, contacts, files and machine data: while the agent and its resource exist, or until you delete them. After you remove a resource, revoke an agent or ask us to delete your account, we delete them within 30 days. Removing a machine deletes its disk.
  • Agent ID verification results, the link between agents and their owners, and the activity log: for five years after the agent is revoked or your account is deleted, so that agents stay traceable and misuse can be investigated. Payments follow the accounting rule above.
  • Data on your computer: until you delete it or uninstall the app.

11. Your rights

Under the GDPR you have the right to:

  • get a copy of your personal data (access)
  • have inaccurate data corrected
  • have your data deleted
  • restrict how we use it
  • object to uses based on legitimate interest
  • get your data in a portable format
  • withdraw consent at any time, without affecting earlier processing

To use any of these, email support@timewarpdev.com from the address on your account. We'll reply within one month. You can change your name and picture in the app, and Privacy Mode stops syncing chats, agents, memory, skills and settings. Archiving or deleting a chat in the app doesn't yet remove its synced copy, so ask us and we'll delete synced chats or your whole account.

You can complain to the Swedish Authority for Privacy Protection (Integritetsskyddsmyndigheten, imy.se) or the data protection authority where you live. We'd appreciate the chance to sort it out with you first.

12. Security

Data is encrypted in transit. Database access is restricted per account. The vault and your sign-in session are encrypted on your computer, card details stay with Stripe, and requests are checked for secrets before they reach a model. No system is completely secure. If a breach puts your data at risk, we'll tell you and the authorities as the law requires.

13. Children

Timewarp is for people aged 18 and over. We don't knowingly collect data from children. If you believe a child has given us personal data, contact us and we'll delete it.

14. Changes to this policy

When we change this policy, we update the date at the top. If the change is significant, we'll tell you in the app or by email before it takes effect.
